speaker: teakabroughm
text: I'm just going to share my screen. Can everyone see the presentation? Yep, we got it. Okay great, thank you. Good evening, Your Worship, Members of Council, and the public. In an effort to reduce the spread of COVID-19, many jurisdictions across Canada and in our region have considered introducing mandatory face coverings in public places. Tonight's presentation will provide information supporting Beaumont Administration's recommended response to mandatory face coverings. On July 30th, Council gave first reading to Bylaw 984-20, Temporary Face Covering Bylaw, and directed Administration to review mandatory face coverings in all public places. Administration subsequently engaged directly with 107 local businesses, reviewed the latest research and health organization recommendations, and considered the public interest of responding to COVID-19 in Beaumont. In addition to the review undertaken by Administration, the context surrounding mandatory face coverings has evolved rapidly. The province has now mandated masks at school for staff and students in grades 4 to 12. The regional approach to mandatory face coverings has not been uniform. Edmonton and St. Albert now require face coverings in all indoor public places. Some municipalities have mandated face coverings in certain public places. Three municipalities have established triggers for mandatory face coverings in all public places, and some municipalities like the City of LaDuke are still considering their response to all mandatory face coverings in all indoor public places. Research shows that when combined with measures such as physical distancing, regular hand washing, and isolating when sick, face coverings in public can be an effective tool to prevent the spread of COVID-19. Research has now been able to discredit common misconceptions around face coverings. Research shows that, for example, wearing a face covering encourages social distancing, does not increase the amount of carbon dioxide an individual breathes in, and does not weaken the immune system. Early research of the effectiveness of face coverings was not conclusive. However, more research has led to international, national, and provincial health organizations and leaders to recommend face coverings be worn in public places. The World Health Organization, Centers for Disease Control, the Public Health Agency of Canada, and Dr. Dina Hinshaw, Alberta's Chief Medical Officer of Health, all recommend people wear face coverings in public. Administration contacted 107 of 167 local businesses in the community that are accessible to the public. 78% of respondents support mandatory face coverings, 18% did not support mandatory face coverings, and 4% of businesses indicated they were indifferent or would maybe support mandatory face coverings. 85% of businesses felt a bylaw would encourage people to wear face coverings while visiting their business. It is important to acknowledge that many held strong preferences regarding mandatory face coverings. The Chamber of Commerce also conducted a survey that was available online. The results vary from the city's survey conducted of local businesses. Beaumont administration was not involved in creating or administering the survey. It was not clear whether IP addresses were tracked to ensure unique responses and responses from local stakeholders. Administration is not able to speak to the reliability of the data or conclusions drawn. Administration did review the comments submitted through the survey and believe many of the concerns identified have been addressed through the proposed bylaw exemptions, research, and the enforcement method proposed. The evolving contacts and administration's review has led administration to recommend Council pass a bylaw mandating face coverings in all indoor public places, rather than only on transit or municipal buildings. This would place Beaumont within option four of our decision matrix, which is shown by the yellow star on the screen. The following provides some rationale for the recommendation. New research shows that face coverings are an effective tool and are not harmful. Face coverings add additional protection against the spread of COVID-19. Proactively mandating face coverings may help keep Beaumont open and encourage members of our community to feel more comfortable accessing services. Administration determined there was strong support from businesses in our city. Administration concluded that it is in the public interest to strive for zero public COVID-19 cases in Beaumont. There is no safe level of COVID-19 cases in the population. An evidence-based model to establish the number of COVID-19 cases that should trigger mandatory face coverings in the community is not available at this time. And removing the distinction between municipal buildings and other public places is more straightforward for the public. It also brings Beaumont in alignment with Edmonton, our largest neighboring municipality. The proposed bylaw includes exemptions for those who are unable to safely wear face coverings, such as young children or those with medical contradictions. The term face covering is used to provide the public with flexibility and simply means any barrier that covers the mouth, nose, and chin. Non-medical masks are currently available in many locations in our community for purchase or free of charge. Although the proposed bylaw does outline fines for extenuating circumstances, the city will take an education-first approach to enforcement. Business owners will not be expected to enforce the bylaw. The city will launch a public awareness and education component. We ask the public to respect the privacy of others. Please do not confront anyone who is not wearing a mask or inquire about any medical condition or disability. The bylaw is temporary. It is proposed to be in effect starting August 14, 2020, until October 31, 2020, and requires a council amendment to extend. In addition, administration will return to council on August 25 with information regarding a potential incentive program to encourage compliance and bring the community together during these difficult times. In closing, Beaumont administration is proposing mandatory face coverings be considered a pragmatic and proactive response to ensure the health and safety of others in the community. City is asking the public to continue to take measures to protect one another as we respond to the COVID-19 pandemic together. This concludes my presentation. Administration is happy to take any questions council may have.
